reader.decision: Approve the 200 MB limit on /api/files in nginx and Flask as the primary fix, with the presigned upload kept as the later alternative.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows that both 10 MB caps cause the 413 errors, that raising them needs no frontend release, and that this meets the Friday 30 October deadline while the frontend team is away until 9 November. The stated load (25 drawings a day, 20 GB buffer, 4 workers) fits the change.

reconstruction.problem: Halvorsen Marine's CAD drawings (60 to 180 MB) cannot be uploaded to pinewood-docs. nginx has client_max_body_size 10m and Flask has MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH at 10 MB.
reconstruction.what_breaks: nginx returns 413 on the Content-Length check before the request reaches pinewood-app. Every drawing from 60 to 180 MB fails, for example the 94 MB one at 09:14:02 and the 160 MB one at 09:31:47.
reconstruction.fix: Add a location = /api/files block in nginx with client_max_body_size 200m and the same proxy_pass and headers as /api/. Raise Flask MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH to 200 MB. No frontend release is needed. The presigned direct-to-bucket upload is the alternative and needs a frontend change.
reconstruction.cost: Each large upload ties up one nginx buffer file and one gunicorn worker for about 3 s. Flask's limit becomes 200 MB globally, but nginx still caps the other endpoints at 10 MB. Files over 200 MB still fail with 413.

follow_up_questions: Does the 30 s gunicorn timeout, or any nginx proxy_read_timeout and client_body_timeout, risk cutting off a 72 s upload? The message says nginx buffers first, but it does not show these timeout settings.
Is the 200 MB ceiling enough? Are any Halvorsen drawings larger than 180 MB?
reader.closing_answer: I approve the 200 MB limit on /api/files in nginx and Flask as the primary fix. I do not want the presigned upload as the primary fix now. I keep it as the follow-up for when files outgrow 200 MB or a frontend release is possible.
